incidents.victim: Latvijas Valsts Mezi (Latvia state forestry company); also pharma firm Olpha/Olainfarm
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a system left unpatched for two years and dwelled on the network for over a week before deploying ransomware and stealing data.
incidents.impact: Mapping, hunting and contractor systems knocked offline; ~44GB of internal documents, email, code, certificates, cryptographic keys and credentials leaked online, with two-thirds of contract customers still without access weeks later. The same actor also compromised a server at pharma firm Olpha.

incidents.victim: Unidentified US organizations (healthcare, manufacturing, education)
incidents.vector: Intrusion via legitimate remote-access software (AnyDesk), then a Microsoft-signed malicious kernel driver (BYOVD) to disable endpoint security, 14 open-source credential-theft tools, and PsExec lateral movement before deploying the ransomware locker.
incidents.impact: A rebranded ransomware-as-a-service crew used a wrongly Microsoft-signed driver to kill security software and entrench in victim networks, harvesting credentials before encryption; Symantec observed the case beginning May 29.

incidents.victim: 142,000+ global fraud victims (individuals, businesses, governments)
incidents.vector: Global law-enforcement action (Interpol Operation First Light) against social-engineering scams — business email compromise, romance, sextortion, impersonation and investment fraud.
incidents.impact: 5,800+ arrests across 97 countries, $293M seized and 31,000+ bank accounts blocked; cases included a suspect who allegedly laundered $122.5M in ten months and a fake police-station scam operation.

incidents.victim: Ransomware-as-a-service gang (disrupted) and 10 other criminal groups
incidents.vector: Canada's Communications Security Establishment ran an offensive cyber operation, with Five Eyes and law-enforcement partners, that disabled the gang's infrastructure and deleted stolen data advertised on the dark web.
incidents.impact: A prolific RaaS group tied to 25+ hacks in Canada had its infrastructure rendered inoperable and its stolen-data listings deleted; CSE also delivered technical disruptions to ten other ransomware groups, per its 2025-26 annual report.

incidents.victim: Organization running an AI gateway to Amazon Bedrock on AWS EC2
incidents.vector: Likely brute-force login to an externally exposed EC2 instance acting as an AI gateway to Amazon Bedrock, followed by deployment of the XMRig Monero miner.
incidents.impact: Confirmed cryptomining on a compromised AI-gateway server that held broad access to models, IAM roles and cloud data; Darktrace framed it as the tip of the iceberg given potential for credential theft and deeper cloud pivoting.

incidents.victim: UK Foreign Office, British embassies and some UK local councils
incidents.vector: Firewall and VPN credentials were harvested during the FortiBleed campaign, which stole credentials from nearly 80,000 Fortinet devices.
incidents.impact: Firewall/VPN credentials granting access to UK Foreign Office, embassy and local-council networks are being sold as a single archive for $60,000, exposing sensitive government network access.

incidents.victim: Unnamed global enterprise (large AWS customer)
incidents.vector: Obtained an AWS access key via a weakness in an internet-facing application, then used agentic AI workflows to chain weaknesses across app services, CI/CD pipelines, source repos and data stores for secrets theft, backdoor creation and exfiltration.
incidents.impact: A lone attacker compromised a large AWS environment in ~72 hours and extorted the victim, performing reversible disruptive actions (blocking S3 access, zeroing ECS capacity, purging queues) as a show of force; Sygnia assessed AI accelerated the operation.

incidents.victim: Taiwanese politicians, academics, journalists and civil society
incidents.vector: Operators used rented LINE accounts registered to Taiwanese numbers to impersonate journalists, build trust, and deliver malware disguised as encrypted communications software.
incidents.impact: A sprawling campaign linked to a CCP-connected Xiamen firm used 100+ malicious domains over nine months to steal credentials and compromise devices; Taiwan issued deferred prosecution orders against two executives who leased the accounts.

incidents.victim: Nayax Ltd. (payments/fintech)
incidents.vector: Unusual activity was detected in one of Nayax's cloud accounts tied to a subsidiary and was blocked and contained.
incidents.impact: Nayax disclosed a contained security event under investigation with US and Israeli law enforcement; scope of data involved is still being determined, and it says core production systems were unaffected.

incidents.victim: US and Canadian universities (physics and engineering research)
incidents.vector: Phishing emails carried a Roundcube webmail exploit chain (CVE-2024-42009 then CVE-2025-49113) to run code in the victim's browser and gain a foothold on the mail server, deploying VShell and webshell persistence.
incidents.impact: Attackers established persistent access to university mail servers to steal data, targeting administrators and professors with national-security links and astrophysics/particle-physics research; Proofpoint assesses the campaign is ongoing with many victims unaware.

incidents.victim: Owners of unpatched Ruckus and ASUS edge routers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known unpatched vulnerabilities in Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy new custom malware (LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH, JARLEASH) and enlist devices into a proxy relay network.
incidents.impact: A China-nexus actor continues expanding operational relay box (ORB) proxy networks on compromised edge devices to mask and route traffic for other Chinese espionage operations against high-value targets.

incidents.victim: KDDI (email platform operated for five Japanese ISPs)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in third-party software used by an email platform KDDI operates for internet service providers.
incidents.impact: More than 12.2 million customer email addresses and 7.6 million passwords were exposed; KDDI patched the flaw and forced ISP password resets, while its own consumer email on separate infrastructure was unaffected.

incidents.victim: ~2 million consumer devices (NetNut / Popa residential proxy botnet)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — residential proxy botnet operator
incidents.vector: Proxy-service SDKs bundled into consumer-device apps silently turned smart TVs and streaming boxes into always-on residential proxy exit nodes with little or no user consent.
incidents.impact: FBI and IRS-CI, with Google and Lumen, seized hundreds of domains tied to the ~2M-device Popa botnet used for ad fraud, scraping, account takeover and password-spray attacks; 316 distinct threat-actor clusters were seen using the exit nodes in one week.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, plus US healthcare providers SSM Health and Sutter Health
incidents.vector: SIM-swapping and voice/SMS phishing to steal employee credentials and MFA codes, enabling network intrusions and ransomware.
incidents.impact: Two members pleaded guilty over the August 2024 attack that crippled Transport for London, with one admitting to hacking US healthcare providers; a US indictment ties one defendant to 120 intrusions across 47 entities and $115M+ in ransoms.

incidents.victim: Consumers and small/medium businesses in the US and EU
incidents.vector: Malvertising lured victims searching for cracked software into downloading loader archives signed with a fabricated code-signing certificate and inflated to ~491MB to evade sandboxes, dropping the Vidar stealer and the XMRig miner.
incidents.impact: Vidar harvested browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets while XMRig mined Monero on victim machines; Unit 42 saw an activity spike in mid-to-late April across US and EU targets.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure providers in the US and Europe
incidents.vector: Hacktivist attacks against critical infrastructure; the arrested individual provided logistical support and took part in operations spreading pro-Russian, anti-Western narratives.
incidents.impact: Spanish police, on an FBI tip under Operation Riptide, arrested an alleged member of the Cyber Army of Russia Reborn and NoName057(16) in Palencia, seizing computers and cryptocurrency; no formal charges have been filed.

incidents.victim: Greek politicians, journalists and former intelligence officials
incidents.vector: Targeting with Intellexa's Predator mercenary surveillance spyware.
incidents.impact: Eight spyware victims sued Intellexa for EUR7.6 million in damages over surveillance of high-profile Greek individuals, with a trial set for next April.

incidents.victim: US Army (multiple public websites)
incidents.vector: Website defacement of multiple US Army web properties.
incidents.impact: Several US Army websites were defaced with political messages targeting the President and the US Ambassador to Turkiye.

incidents.victim: BONK meme-coin holders and protocol
incidents.vector: A malicious governance attack transferred 4.4 trillion BONK tokens to attacker-controlled wallets.
incidents.impact: Roughly $20 million in crypto-assets stolen; exchanges Upbit and Kraken paused BONK transactions while the hack is investigated.

incidents.victim: Bandai Channel (anime streaming service)
incidents.vector: Exploited a vulnerability in Bandai Channel servers to fraudulently cancel user subscriptions.
incidents.impact: More than 46,000 user subscriptions were fraudulently cancelled; Tokyo police arrested a 15-year-old suspect.

incidents.victim: Users of less-common mobile crypto software wallets
incidents.vector: The 'Ill Bloom' weakness let attackers recover a wallet's private key from its public address due to weak randomness in address generation.
incidents.impact: More than $3.1 million in cryptocurrency was stolen from wallets whose private keys were predictable, per Coinspect.

incidents.victim: Ctrl Wallet users (Cardano-based multi-chain wallet)
incidents.vector: The multi-chain wallet was hit by an exploit in late June, one of several Cardano-based wallets struck by similar attacks.
incidents.impact: Following undisclosed losses, Ctrl Wallet announced it will shut down on August 3 and told users to withdraw funds within a month.

incidents.victim: US and international government, military, media officials, and Ukrainian officials
incidents.vector: Phishing messages masqueraded as automated messaging-app support to trick victims into surrendering backup recovery keys, verification codes and account PINs for Signal and WhatsApp.
incidents.impact: An ongoing Russian intelligence campaign hijacks individual messaging-app accounts (without breaking encryption), letting attackers read historical private and group messages; FBI and CISA updated their joint public advisory.

incidents.victim: John Bolton (former US National Security Advisor) / US national defense information
incidents.vector: An Iran-linked actor hacked Bolton's personal email account, into which he had transmitted classified diary entries, after he left office.
incidents.impact: Iran-linked hackers accessed a personal email containing TOP SECRET/SCI material; Bolton pleaded guilty to willfully retaining national defense information and faces up to 60 months and a $2.25M fine.
